guideTitle: 6 Best Ultrasonic Cleaners for Jewelry in 2026
metaDescription: We compared six ultrasonic jewelry cleaners on frequency, tank size, timer presets and cooling, to help you pick an easy machine for rings, chains and glasses.
introParagraphs: Rings, chains and earrings collect skin oil, lotion and soap film in the places a cloth cannot reach, and scrubbing those settings with a small brush is tiring on the hands. An ultrasonic cleaner does that work for you by filling the water with microscopic bubbles that lift grime out of prongs, links and engraving. The catch is that the tubs look alike online while their frequency, tank size and timer options differ quite a bit.

We evaluated six jewelry-sized machines based on product specs and buyer feedback, looking at ultrasonic frequency, tank capacity, how many timer presets each offers, whether it has a cooling fan or degassing step, and how simple the controls are. Frequencies in this lineup run from 42,000 Hz to 48 kHz, and tanks run from 350 ml to 800 ml, so the right machine depends on whether you clean a few rings or a mix of jewelry and eyeglasses.

Read the picks first, then use the buying criteria and decision tables to match one to your pieces. Keep in mind that soft stones such as pearls and opals, and anything with a loose setting, should stay out of any ultrasonic tub.

products.name: Magnasonic 20oz Stainless Steel Ultrasonic Cleaner
products.description:
The Magnasonic is the most balanced machine in this group. It runs at 42,000 Hz and holds 20 oz (600 ml) in an anti-corrosion stainless tank, which is enough for several rings, a chain or a pair of glasses at a time. A digital display lets you choose one of five cycles, from a quick refresh to a deeper clean.

The five cycles take the guesswork out of timing, and the included basket keeps pieces off the tank floor. The listing states plainly that it does not remove tarnish, which is worth believing, because tarnish is a surface chemical change and not dirt. It has no heater, so heavy oil relies on time rather than warmth.

Setup is simply tap water to the fill line, a cycle choice and a lift of the basket when it finishes. Against the 350 ml OSLTWI it holds noticeably more, while the 800 ml VisiClean offers extra room and a second transducer. It is the pick we would hand to most households that want one dependable tub.
products.bestFor: Households that want one dependable machine for jewelry, glasses and small everyday items.
pros: The 42,000 Hz output is a good fit for rings, chains and eyeglass frames
Five preset cycles take the guesswork out of how long to run a clean
The 600 ml stainless tank holds several rings or one pair of glasses
The included basket keeps pieces off the tank floor and easy to lift out
cons: There is no heater, so greasy buildup relies on time and a mild solution
It will not remove tarnish from silver, which needs a polish instead
The tank is too small for large watch bands or bulky tool trays

products.name: VisiClean 800 ml Dual Transducer Ultrasonic Cleaner
products.description:
The VisiClean pairs 42,000 Hz output with two ultrasonic transducers, which the listing says doubles the cleaning power of a single-transducer tub. Its 800 ml (27 oz) stainless tank is the largest here, and it adds a cooling fan, touch controls and a waterproofed interior. Five preset settings cover short refreshes through heavier jobs.

The lid is removable and non-hinged and the power cord detaches, so filling, rinsing and storing are easier than on fixed-cord tubs. The maker advises against hot water and against running longer than 30 minutes, which is sensible because small units warm up. It is more machine than a simple ring rinse needs, and it takes more shelf space.

In use you fill with cool water, choose a preset and let it run. Its extra room handles glasses, bracelets and watch bands that the 350 ml OSLTWI cannot take, and it holds 200 ml more than the 600 ml Magnasonic. Against the 600 ml LifeBasis, the main difference is the second transducer.
products.bestFor: Anyone cleaning bracelets, glasses and several rings at once who wants stronger output.
pros: Dual transducers add cleaning power while staying at a gentle 42,000 Hz
The 800 ml tank is the roomiest in this lineup for bracelets and glasses
A detachable cord and removable lid make filling and storing easier
A built-in cooling fan helps the unit cope with longer cleaning runs
cons: The maker advises no hot water, so there is no warm clean option
It should not run past 30 minutes at a stretch, so plan short cycles
It is bulkier than the compact tubs for a drawer or small shelf

products.name: LifeBasis 600 ml 45kHz Ultrasonic Jewelry Cleaner
products.description:
The LifeBasis runs at 45,000 Hz with 35W transducers in a 600 ml SUS 304 stainless tank. Five presets of 90, 180, 300, 480 and 600 seconds let you pick a time with auto shut off, and the touch buttons sit beside a digital display. It also starts every cycle with a 20-second degassing step that removes air bubbles from the water before the real work begins.

The listing says it is the only household machine with a built-in cooling fan, plus overheating protection, which suits people who like to run a couple of cycles back to back. That is a manufacturer claim, so we weighed it as a feature and not a ranking. The tradeoff is that 45,000 Hz is a touch gentler than the Magnasonic at 42,000 Hz, so heavy grime may need a second pass.

The cord is removable, which makes filling and storing less awkward, and the 600 ml tank matches the Magnasonic's size. Compared with the onlikin at 480 seconds maximum, it offers a longer 600-second preset for stubborn buildup. It makes a good choice for anyone who wants a longer timer without much fuss.
products.bestFor: Jewelry owners who want automatic degassing, a cooling fan and a long 600 second preset.
pros: A 20-second degas step runs before every cycle to clear air from the water
Five presets from 90 to 600 seconds include a long cycle for stubborn film
The built-in cooling fan and overheat protection suit repeat cycles
The removable power cord makes filling and putting the tub away easier
cons: At 45,000 Hz it is gentler than the 42,000 Hz models on heavy grime
The 600 ml tank is too small for larger bracelets or chunky watch bands
Maker claims on the cooling fan are unverified, so treat them as a bonus

products.name: onlikin 35W 45kHz Ultrasonic Jewelry Cleaner, 20 oz
products.description:
The onlikin is the only pick here that lets you change the power. It offers three power levels at 45,000 Hz and 35W, so a delicate pair of earrings can get a lighter setting than a sturdy watch strap. A digital display with touch control shows five timers of 90, 180, 300, 420 and 480 seconds, and the 480-second mode adds a degassing step.

The 20 oz tank is 304 stainless steel, and the listing rates the noise at under 38 dB, the quietest claim among the six. That is helpful in a shared home or a quiet kitchen. The downside is that three power levels plus five timers means more buttons to learn than the one-touch machines, and it has no heater or basket detail in the listing.

Day to day it is a fill, tap and wait routine, and you can rerun the short cycle on pieces that look fine at first. Next to the 350 ml KUNPHY it holds far more, and against the LifeBasis it trades the fan for power control. We like it for people who own a mix of sturdy and delicate pieces.
products.bestFor: Owners of mixed jewelry who want a lighter setting for delicate pieces and a quiet tub.
pros: Three power levels let you go lighter on earrings and stronger on bands
Five timers from 90 to 480 seconds cover quick refreshes and deep cleans
Listed at under 38 dB, it is the quietest claim in this lineup
The 480-second mode adds a degassing step before the main wash
cons: Three power levels and five timers add more buttons to learn at first
The listing mentions no cooling fan, so avoid back-to-back long cycles
It tops out at 480 seconds, shorter than the 600-second LifeBasis

products.name: OSLTWI 48kHz Ultrasonic Jewelry Cleaner, 350 ml
products.description:
The OSLTWI uses the highest frequency in the group at 48 kHz, which is the gentlest end of the range for fine rings, earrings and thin eyeglass frames. Its 304 stainless tank holds 350 ml, and the whole machine weighs just 0.57 kg. A single one-touch selector switches between two cleaning modes.

The small tank is the honest tradeoff, since several rings or a pair of glasses fit but bracelets and wide watch bands do not. With two modes you also get less control than the five-preset Magnasonic or LifeBasis, which is fine for a quick weekly refresh of daily-wear pieces. The listing leans on marketing claims, so we focused on the plain specs of frequency, tank, weight and mode count.

Because it is light and compact it can sit in a drawer and come out for a weekly clean. Fill with water, press the button and rinse the pieces. Compared with the 800 ml VisiClean it gives up capacity for a much smaller footprint, and it has the same 350 ml tank as the KUNPHY at a higher frequency.
products.bestFor: Light jewelry cleaning where a small, simple, gentle machine is enough.
pros: At 48 kHz it is the gentlest frequency here, ideal for fine, delicate pieces
Weighs only 0.57 kg, so it tucks into a drawer between weekly uses
A one-touch mode selector keeps operation simple for any user
The 304 stainless tank resists wear, scratches and corrosion
cons: The 350 ml tank is too small for bracelets, bulky glasses or watch bands
Only two cleaning modes, so less control than the five-preset models
No cooling fan or detailed timer settings to tune each cycle

products.name: KUNPHY 46kHz Ultrasonic Jewelry Cleaner, 350 ml
products.description:
The KUNPHY is the plainest machine in this comparison. It uses 46,000 Hz sound waves, has a key touch control and runs a fixed 3-minute timer, so you press once and walk away. The 350 ml tank is enough for eyeglasses, rings and necklaces, and the listing puts operating noise below 45 dB.

That simplicity is also the limit, because there are no alternative cycles for stubborn film and no mention of a basket, cooling fan or degas step. Three minutes handles routine oil and lotion on daily-wear pieces, but heavier buildup may need a second run. The listing notes that the black tarnish on silver is normal oxidation and needs a different treatment.

It is small enough for travel, and the one-year quality commitment gives the buyer some reassurance. Compared with the OSLTWI at 48 kHz it is a touch lower in frequency but shares the same 350 ml size, and against the onlikin it swaps adjustable power for a no-decision button. Choose it as a first machine or a gift.
products.bestFor: First-time buyers and gift givers who want a single button and a short fixed cycle.
pros: A single touch starts a fixed 3-minute cycle with no settings to learn
The 46,000 Hz output is gentle enough for daily-wear rings and chains
Operating noise is listed below 45 dB for use in a shared home
Small enough to travel with and covered by a one-year commitment
cons: One fixed 3-minute cycle means heavier buildup needs a second run
The 350 ml tank cannot take bracelets, bulky glasses or watch bands
It will not lift tarnish, which the listing calls normal oxidation

buyingCriteria.explanation: Frequency controls how harsh the bubbles are, with lower numbers producing larger, more aggressive cavitation. Around 40 kHz suits tools, while 42 kHz and above is the more comfortable range for rings, chains and thin eyeglass frames. In this lineup the Magnasonic and VisiClean run at 42,000 Hz, the LifeBasis and onlikin at 45,000 Hz, the KUNPHY at 46,000 Hz and the OSLTWI at 48 kHz. For fine or older pieces, lean toward the OSLTWI or KUNPHY, and treat frequency figures as manufacturer claims.

The tank decides what you can clean in one go, and pieces must sit in the liquid without touching the walls. About 350 ml suits a few rings and glasses, 600 ml adds necklaces and small watch bands, and 800 ml helps with bracelets. The OSLTWI and KUNPHY hold 350 ml, the Magnasonic and LifeBasis hold 600 ml and the VisiClean holds 800 ml. Measure your largest bracelet or glasses frame before you choose, and size up if you clean for a household.

Presets matter because over-cleaning delicate items is easier than most people expect, and a guess at the minutes rarely helps. Three to five minutes is a normal jewelry cycle, and longer settings are for stubborn film. The Magnasonic and VisiClean offer five presets, the LifeBasis offers five from 90 to 600 seconds, the onlikin five from 90 to 480 seconds, the OSLTWI two modes and the KUNPHY one 3-minute cycle. Pick more presets if different family members share the tub.

Some machines let you change power or remove dissolved air first, and both can improve results on tight settings. Fresh tap water holds air that dampens the bubbles, which is why a degas step helps in the first minute. The onlikin offers three power levels and a degassing step in its 480-second mode, and the LifeBasis runs a 20-second degas before every cycle. For delicate and sturdy pieces owned together, an adjustable tub like the onlikin is more forgiving than a fixed-output model.

A small tub warms up as it runs, and heat can stress glued stones and some plastics. Short cycles of a few minutes are normal, and long continuous runs overheat small units. The VisiClean and LifeBasis both include a cooling fan, and the VisiClean maker advises no hot water and no run beyond 30 minutes. If you clean often, a fan model protects the machine, while the KUNPHY and OSLTWI are best kept to their short built-in cycles.

Ultrasonic cleaning is not safe for every piece, and no machine changes that. Soft or porous stones such as pearls, opals, turquoise and emeralds can crack or cloud, and treated stones, loose stones and worn prongs can shake free. Tarnish is chemical, so the Magnasonic and KUNPHY listings say they do not remove it. If you own delicate or antique pieces, use the 48 kHz OSLTWI at most, and ask a jeweler about anything valuable.

howWeEvaluated.title: Frequency and cleaning power
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared stated frequency, transducer count and wattage across the six tubs. The VisiClean leads on raw strength with two transducers at 42,000 Hz, while the OSLTWI leads on gentleness at 48 kHz. The onlikin and LifeBasis both list 35W at 45,000 Hz. All figures are manufacturer claims, so we weighed them against buyer feedback.

howWeEvaluated.title: Tank size and practicality
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at tank volume, material and how easy each unit is to fill, empty and store. The VisiClean holds 800 ml, the Magnasonic and LifeBasis 600 ml, and the OSLTWI and KUNPHY 350 ml. Removable lids, detachable cords and included baskets earned extra credit.

howWeEvaluated.title: Controls and timer presets
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared how many cycles each machine offers and how easy they are to read and choose. The Magnasonic, VisiClean, LifeBasis and onlikin each give five presets, the OSLTWI gives two modes and the KUNPHY one cycle. We judged whether the controls suit a first-time user.

howWeEvaluated.title: Item safety and thermal management
howWeEvaluated.description: We checked what each maker says about hot water, run time, cooling and unsuitable items. The VisiClean and LifeBasis include cooling fans, the VisiClean advises a 30-minute limit, and the Magnasonic and KUNPHY state they do not remove tarnish. We weighted this guidance heavily.

howWeEvaluated.title: Ownership and value
howWeEvaluated.description: We considered noise, weight and the feature set for each machine's class. The onlikin lists under 38 dB, the OSLTWI weighs 0.57 kg, and the KUNPHY lists a one-year quality commitment. We did not rank on price, only on what each model offers for its position in the lineup.

faq.q: Which ultrasonic jewelry cleaner is best for most people?
faq.a: For most households the Magnasonic is the safest all-round pick, with 42,000 Hz output, a 600 ml stainless tank and five cycles. If you have bracelets or clean for a family, the 800 ml VisiClean with two transducers has more room. If you only clean a ring or two, the 350 ml OSLTWI at 48 kHz is simpler and lighter.

faq.q: Is a higher frequency better for jewelry?
faq.a: Higher frequency is gentler rather than stronger, because it produces smaller bubbles. The OSLTWI at 48 kHz suits fine and delicate pieces, while the 42,000 Hz Magnasonic and VisiClean hit grime a little harder. Tank design and power matter as much as the number, so use the figure as a rough guide.

faq.q: Which stones should never go in an ultrasonic cleaner?
faq.a: Avoid pearls, opals, turquoise, emeralds, amber and coral, which can crack, cloud or lose their finish. Treated or fracture-filled stones, loose stones and worn prongs can also shake free. Watches that are not water resistant should stay out. If you are unsure, ask a jeweler before running a cycle.

faq.q: Will an ultrasonic cleaner remove tarnish from silver?
faq.a: No, because tarnish is a chemical change on the surface and not dirt. The Magnasonic and KUNPHY listings both say they do not remove tarnish, and the KUNPHY calls it normal oxidation. Use a silver polish or dip for tarnish, then use the tub for the remaining oil and film.

faq.q: Do I need a cleaning solution, or is water enough?
faq.a: Water alone handles light daily dirt, and the OSLTWI listing is built around a water-only approach. A few drops of a mild jewelry-safe solution help with lotion and oil buildup, if your manual allows it. Never use harsh chemicals or hot water unless the maker says the unit supports it. The VisiClean maker, for example, advises against hot water.

faq.q: How long should I run each cycle?
faq.a: Three to five minutes is normal for everyday jewelry, which is why the KUNPHY uses a fixed 3-minute cycle. Longer settings such as the LifeBasis at 600 seconds or the onlikin at 480 seconds are for stubborn film. Long continuous runs can overheat small units, so keep to the maker's limits, such as 30 minutes at most on the VisiClean.

faq.q: How do I keep the machine working for years?
faq.a: Empty and dry the tank after each use, and never run it without liquid. Use the basket so pieces do not rest on the tank floor, and wipe the control panel with a damp cloth rather than spraying it. A detachable cord and removable lid, as on the VisiClean and LifeBasis, make cleaning easier. Let a fan-cooled unit rest between long runs.
